chunks: Jābir narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:

Whoever conceals testimony, or testifies by it so as to unlawfully shed the blood of a Muslim man or to destroy the wealth of a Muslim man, shall come on the Day of Resurrection with darkness upon his face as far as the eye can see, and on his face will be scars by which the creatures will know him by his name and lineage. And whoever gives a true testimony in order to preserve thereby the wealth of a Muslim man shall come on the Day of Resurrection with light upon his face as far as the eye can see; the creatures will know him by his name and lineage.
Then Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: Do you not see that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
And establish the testimony for Allah.

key_terms.الشَّهَادَةَ: testimony or witness-bearing in a legal and moral sense
key_terms.الْخَلَائِقُ: the creatures, meaning all creation who will recognize such a person
key_terms.دَمَ: blood, referring here to unlawful killing or bloodshed
key_terms.ظُلْمَةٌ: darkness appearing as a mark of disgrace and punishment
key_terms.كَتَمَ: concealed or withheld what should be disclosed
key_terms.مَالَ: property or wealth that must be protected from wrongful loss
key_terms.نُورٌ: light appearing as a mark of honor and reward
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection when people are judged

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about concealing testimony or giving false testimony against a Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith condemns concealing testimony and giving testimony that leads to wrongful bloodshed or the loss of another Muslim's property. It also praises truthful testimony that protects the rights of others, linking this moral and legal duty to the Qur'anic command to establish testimony sincerely for Allah.
